newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: VW's February sales up 13 percent.
newsitem.headline: VW's February sales up 13 percent.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said Tuesday its sales rose 13 percent to about 660,000 vehicles in February and that sales so far for the year were doing well.

VW management board member Robert Buechelhofer told Reuters in an interview at the Geneva car show that sales in the critical western European market were up about 7 to 8 percent for the month over the year-ago period.

But he said sales were down about 4 to 6 percent in Germany during February, in part due to the suspension of production for about a week of VW's Polo model due to parts shortages caused by the Spanish trucker's strike.

Buechelhofer noted that incoming orders in Germany for the first two months of 1997 were up 30 percent. "Incoming orders in Germany are going very well and have been above our expectations," he said. "The situation in Germany will work itself out."
He declined to provide forecasts for 1997 VW sales, saying "it would be speculative to talk about the full year."
But Buechelhofer noted that he expected VW to maintain the worldwide market share of about 10 percent, achieved in 1996, despite weakening consumer demand for vehicles.
VW said provisional sales results for February showed eastern European sales rose 30 percent, while North American sales rose 27 percent.
In South America and Africa combined, the carmaker's sales were up 17 percent. Sales in the Asia-Pacific region rose 28 percent, including a 34 percent increase in sales in Japan.
The carmaker did not provide specific sales figures for the month.
